skill.name: elevenlabs-music-generation
skill.description: Generate full songs, instrumental tracks, jingles, podcast intros, and game loops with ElevenLabs Music through the RunComfy CLI. The skill prepares structured prompts, duration settings, instrumental options, and output guidance for 5-second to 5-minute audio renders.
skill.summary: Generate structured songs and instrumental tracks with ElevenLabs Music through RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting or documentation links and are false positives, not Ruby backtick execution. The confirmed risks are expected RunComfy CLI execution and third-party API submission of prompts and lyrics; no prompt injection attempt or malicious hidden-file behavior was found.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is required for generation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep allowed tools limited to runcomfy commands and request user confirmation before cost-bearing generations.

remediation.issue: Prompts and lyrics are sent to a third-party API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit secrets, unreleased lyrics, or copyrighted material without rights and approval.

remediation.issue: The setup guidance includes npm and npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly label package manager commands as manual setup and avoid running them automatically from the skill.

remediation.issue: RunComfy token storage is documented in the user home config directory.
remediation.suggestion: Keep advising mode 0600 storage, environment variables in CI, and never logging or prompting with the token.

content.user_title: Generate Music with ElevenLabs on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Creating structured songs from a text brief usually requires separate music tools and manual setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to call RunComfy with prompts, durations, and output settings.
actual_capabilities: Generate full songs and instrumental tracks through the RunComfy CLI.
Prepare style briefs with lyrics, sections, tempo, mood, and instruments.
Set music duration from 5 seconds to 5 minutes per request.
Request instrumental-only output with the force_instrumental option.
Download generated 44.1 kHz stereo audio into a chosen output directory.
Use RunComfy exit code guidance for common CLI failures.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, account access, a token, and network connectivity.
Each generation request is limited to 5 minutes of audio.
Does not provide sound effects, text-to-speech, voice cloning, or specific singer control.
Does not verify lyric rights, confidential content, or downstream commercial obligations.

use_cases.title: Create a Video Theme Song
use_cases.description: Generate a structured intro, verse, and chorus that match a video length and mood.

use_cases.title: Produce a Podcast Intro Bed
use_cases.description: Create a short instrumental opening with a clean ending and consistent tone.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multilingual Campaign Music
use_cases.description: Reuse one style brief while swapping lyric languages for campaign drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Instrumental
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 30-second calm instrumental bed for a tutorial video. Use warm piano, soft drums, and no vocals.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Structured Song Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with sections and vocal direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 45-second upbeat pop song draft with intro, verse, chorus, female vocal, 120 BPM, and simple original lyrics.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Brand Jingle
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 10-second instrumental brand jingle with bright marimba, light percussion, a clean final chord, and no vocals.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Iterative Music Production
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for testing and final rendering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare three 35-second draft options for a game loop, then recommend one final 90-second instrumental render.

output_examples.input: Need a calm lo-fi background track for a study video.
output_examples.output: A generation brief with lo-fi style, warm keys, soft drums, instrumental mode, 90-second duration, and an output folder.

output_examples.input: Need a short jingle for a product launch bumper.
output_examples.output: A concise music plan with cheerful instruments, 5-second length, no vocals, and a clean ending for video editing.

output_examples.input: Need a vocal song draft with verse and chorus sections.
output_examples.output: A structured prompt that includes genre, tempo, vocal type, section markers, original lyrics, and a draft render duration.

best_practices: Start with a short draft before paying for a long render.
Include genre, mood, tempo, instruments, vocal type, and section markers.
Confirm rights and privacy before sending lyrics or brand material to the API.
anti_patterns: Sending secrets, unreleased lyrics, or copyrighted text without permission.
Mixing contradictory styles, moods, or vocal directions in one request.
Using this skill for sound effects, speech synthesis, or voice cloning tasks.

faq.question: Does this skill generate the audio directly inside the assistant?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to use the local RunComfy CLI and the ElevenLabs Music model.

faq.question: What do I need before using it?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, valid account access, and a configured token or environment variable.

faq.question: Can it create instrumental tracks?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports instrumental output by setting instrumental mode and describing no vocals in the prompt.

faq.question: How long can one generated track be?
faq.answer: One request can generate audio from 5 seconds to 5 minutes.

faq.question: Can it clone a singer or choose a specific voice?
faq.answer: No. This endpoint does not expose voice cloning or specific singer identity controls.

faq.question: Where does the generated audio go?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads the generated audio into the output directory selected for the request.
